verdict: OK to lend in Nashik electrical equipment, pumps and motors — pursue export-linked component and specialty-motor makers with tight monthly discipline; avoid power-intensive, low-margin assemblers exposed to the MERC tariff change.
title: Nashik Electrical Equipment, Pumps & Motors: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**These units buy steel, copper, laminations and bought-out components, wind them and assemble them into motors, pumps and switchgear, then sell into agriculture, construction, railways and export OEMs.** Cash comes back through dealer networks and OEM receivables, not over the counter. Value sits in the winding and testing shop, not the shed; the real cash sits in receivables and inventory of copper and finished pumps. **So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days by buyer type and the copper inventory holding; if finished-goods days exceed the sector norm, ask what is unsold and why.**
**So size the drawing power on a realistic cycle, not the peak; if the customer asks for a limit above his peak receivable-plus-inventory need, ask him to bring the buyer-wise ageing.**

## What has changed now
**Two local facts cut against each other.** Maharashtra GST collections rose 8.6% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D], and all-India electrical equipment (NIC 27) output is up 30.9% YoY with exports up 19.8% Apr-to-date in USD [D] — demand is real. But MERC's seven new electricity regulations have Nashik industry worried about power cost, with NIMA flagging the burden [2], and Dindori supply is already under stress [3]. **So when a proposal lands, check the unit's power cost as a share of conversion cost; if it is a high-consumption heat-treatment or melting operation, ask for the last three electricity bills and the MERC tariff category.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2 component and specialty-motor suppliers feeding railways, wind and off-highway OEMs — the segment Pitti Engineering calls out as valuable in complex applications [4] — and export-linked pump makers riding the 19.8% export growth [D].** Avoid pure assembly units with thin margins and heavy power draw. **Take every month: buyer-wise ageing, GST returns, electricity bills and a stock statement; if any one is late twice, freeze the limit.**

**So if a borrower's revenue grows but PAT margin slips below 6% (Shakti's Q1 FY27 level [6]), ask for the price list and the top-three buyer contracts.** Note the rating reports [8][9][10] are undated or old — treat them as background, not current. Nashik-specific data is thin; lean on these first principles and peers.
